hypothesis: Funding on two venues for the same coin differs because their rate formulas and trader bases differ (Hyperliquid adds a fixed ~11%/yr interest leg; dYdX v4 has its own). Shorting the perp on the richer venue and longing it on the cheaper one is delta-neutral with no spot leg and collects the spread. Rule: per coin, each week, trailing funding spread s = HL - dYdX (annualized, through yesterday); hold short-rich/long-cheap when |s| on capital (|s| x L/2, since both legs post 1/L margin) beats the T-bill yield, else T-bills. Universe: the point-in-time Hyperliquid top 20 intersected with dYdX markets (k-prefixed HL tickers mapped to their dYdX names). Costs: 8bp per leg per trade, daily margin top-up on both legs, liquidation of either leg when the day's high (short leg) or low (long leg) moves 1/L - 3% from the prior close, 5% penalty base with 2% and 10% sensitivities. Sample starts 2024-01-01 to skip dYdX v4's launch period of zero rates. Variants: leverage {2x, 3x} x lookback {7, 30}. PRIMARY, named now: 2x, 30 days. Pass for a defensible out-of-sample 1.5, as with strategy 21: Sharpe after 5% liquidations >= 1.5, PSR(SR>0) >= 0.95, and also >= 1.5 in 2025-26 alone since decay killed the single-venue carry. Also reported: how much of the spread is Hyperliquid's interest constant.
name: crypto cross-venue funding dispersion (Hyperliquid vs dYdX v4)
note: re-declared from edge-audit strategy 25 (declared there at the same time, before any data was pulled); closed there as transferred

FAILS all three declared criteria. primary (2x, 30d) after 5% liquidations: 1.1% excess over T-bills, sharpe 0.39, PSR(>0) 0.71, 2024 sharpe 2.77, 2025-26 -0.36. 3x variants -1.66/-1.73. the raw spread short HL / long dYdX is mostly hyperliquid's 11% interest constant (spread ex-interest -1.6%, -10.6%, -12.6% in 2024/25/26) and decays 9.3% to 0.3% to -1.7%. BUT the rule picks direction and the dispersion it captures is real and persistent: with nothing charged, 6.5% excess and sharpe 3.69, 3.82 in 2025-26. the declared costs eat 5.5 points, split about evenly: switching/entry (8bp/leg) ~2.0, daily collateral top-up ~1.8, liquidation penalty ~1.8. so the gross edge exists and execution cost decides the trade. any cheaper-execution variant designed now has seen this data and is in-sample

hypothesis: Strategy 25 found real Hyperliquid-dYdX funding dispersion (gross Sharpe 3.69, 3.82 in 2025-26) that its declared execution costs consumed. This spec cuts those costs, and it was designed AFTER seeing that breakdown, so its backtest is in-sample and counts for nothing; only the forward record is evidence. SPEC, frozen in models/xv_v1.json with a hash of forward_xv.py: universe = weekly top 20 Hyperliquid perps by trailing 30-day notional that also list on dYdX; signal = trailing 30-day funding spread HL minus dYdX, annualized; 2x leverage on both legs (capital = notional); hysteresis: enter in the spread's direction when |spread| on capital > T-bill + 2%, exit when it falls below T-bill, flip only if it clears the entry band the other way; reviewed weekly at the Monday 00:00 UTC run. Costs: 3bp per leg per trade (resting orders), collateral moves 1bp of the amount moved (daily |return|), liquidation of either leg when the day's high or low moves 47% from the prior close, 5% penalty. Equal capital per universe coin; sleeves not held sit in T-bills. PASS at 52 live weeks: annualized Sharpe of weekly excess >= 1.5 AND PSR(SR > 0) >= 0.95. Interim look at 26 weeks is report-only. KILL: stop and record if cumulative live excess falls below -5% of capital.
name: cross-venue dispersion, forward test (xv_v1)

about: out-of-time test of strategies 20, 21, 24 on BitMEX 2017-2023
rule: Whatever the out-of-time window says is reported as the headline for the bear-market question, including if it is better than the Hyperliquid result. No window trimming: the window is fixed above.
statement: Every carry result so far comes from Hyperliquid, May 2023 onward: no bear market. BitMEX serves perpetual funding since 2016 (XBTUSD) and 2018 (ETHUSD), and spot index prices (.BXBT, .BETH) since 2017. Applying the EXISTING rules unchanged to time before the Hyperliquid sample is an out-of-time holdout for hypotheses already declared, not a new trial. Universe: BTC and ETH perps on BitMEX, equal capital, ETH from its first funding date. Window for the HEADLINE: from the first day with both funding and spot index (2017-03) through 2023-04-30, i.e. strictly before the Hyperliquid sample; 2023-05 onward reported separately for continuity only. Rules, with the exact parameters already declared: strategy 20 always-on carry at 3x; strategy 21 switched (30-day trailing funding vs T-bills, weekly, 3x); strategy 24 equal-weight 2x and its primary (inverse-vol 2x), gate off. Same cost model as validate.py: 8bp per leg, daily margin top-up, liquidation when the day high clears the prior close by 1/L - 3% with a 5% penalty, basis from perp vs spot index closes, T-bills from FRED DTB3. BitMEX XBTUSD and ETHUSD are inverse/quanto contracts; they are modeled as linear USD positions so the rule is tested, not the contract design. Pass for a defensible 1.5: Sharpe after liquidations >= 1.5 over the out-of-time window, and positive excess in each bear year (2018 and 2022) reported as a separate check.

about: out-of-time test of strategies 20, 21, 24 on BitMEX 2017-2023
action: out_of_time.py prints both versions, precommitted first. the corrected one is the result.
verdict: FAILS, and the precommitted headline is wrong because the precommitment was. It modeled BitMEX ETHUSD, a quanto contract settled in BTC, as a linear USD position. A daily-rebalanced short quanto hedged with spot ETH carries a cross-term of -(r_eth x r_btc); over the window that cost 57.8% a year against 57.3% of funding (net -0.5%). The funding was the price of the quanto risk, not a carry, and the as-precommitted Sharpes of 1.59 to 2.15 are that error. Corrected, every spec is about zero (-0.15 to 0.08) and loses money in both bear years (2018 -5% to -10%, 2022 -5% to -8%). BTC alone, the clean inverse contract, gives 0.37 switched and 0.51 at 2x, the same picture as Hyperliquid. The carry does not survive the bear markets it had never seen.

statement: First order-book snapshot, 2026-10-12, for the 16 coins xv_v1 holds in its first live week. Hyperliquid is liquid (median half-spread 0.7bp, ~7bp to take $10k with fees, ~12bp for $100k). dYdX v4 is not: median half-spread 35bp, 42bp to take $10k, 214bp for $100k. dYdX 24h volume is $3m on BTC and under $0.05m on 14 of the 16 coins, with zero trades on XPL and LIT; dYdX open interest is under $0.3m on every held coin except BTC and SOL. Much of the dYdX side of the funding spread is set in markets almost nobody trades. The frozen spec assumes 3bp per leg and has NO capacity filter, so xv_v1 can pass its rule on positions that could not be put on at meaningful size. Recorded now, before any scored week, so that whatever the forward result, it is read together with exec_costs.jsonl. The spec is not changed: changing it would be xv_v2, a new trial.
